history.p: The myth about Agnete and the Merman fascinated Gade in his early youth. While he was travelling in Sweden in September 1838, he started working on an overture, which he abandoned. A year later he laid the framework for an even more ambitious work on the same theme: a symphony in five parts with choir. The work never materialized. But then he met Hans Christian Andersen who as early as 1833 had written an ill-fated poem on the theme, and together they set out to write a play with incidental music. The first performance was a failure and after the second performance it was taken off the bill.

incipText.p: Der voxed et Træ i min Moders Gaard
Jeg veed et Slot dets Væg og Tag
Agnete kjend mig i din Drøm
Agnete var elsket, uskyldig og god
Den fattige Fugl sad paa Grenen og sang
Barn Jesus, Brudgom faur og fiin
For Dig vort Knæ vi bøie!
Død er hun, død Agnete og jordet hendes Been
